abhiman: (Sanskrit) the proud, wounded anger felt when someone you love hurts or neglects you.
acedia: a restless, listless apathy — the noonday boredom and spiritual weariness once thought to afflict monks.
amae: (Japanese) the warm sense of leaning on another's love, of being able to depend on and be indulged by them.
ambiguphobia: an urge to avoid ambiguity — a discomfort with the vague, uncertain or open-ended.
anger: the hot, aroused response to being wronged, thwarted or threatened.
anticipation: the excited, forward-leaning expectation of something about to happen.
anxiety: an uneasy dread about an uncertain future; worry without a clear object.
apathy: an absence of feeling or motivation; indifference and listlessness.
appel-du-vide: (French, 'the call of the void') the sudden, vertiginous urge to leap when standing somewhere high.
awumbuk: (Baining, Papua New Guinea) the heavy emptiness that settles over a house after guests depart.
bafflement: the puzzled state of being unable to make sense of something.
basorexia: a sudden, overwhelming urge to kiss someone.
bewilderment: the disoriented feeling of being utterly lost or perplexed.
boredom: weary restlessness at the tedium of an unstimulating present.
brabant: the mischievous urge to needle someone to see how far you can push them.
broodiness: an aching, bodily longing to have and hold a baby.
calm: a tranquil, untroubled stillness of mind.
carefree: light and untroubled, free of worry or responsibility.
claustrophobia: the panic of being confined in a cramped or enclosed space.
collywobbles: the fluttering, queasy nerves felt in the stomach before a big moment.
comfort: the soothing ease of being consoled and reassured.
compassion: a tender concern for another's suffering, and the wish to relieve it.
compersion: the warm joy felt at a loved one's happiness with someone else — the opposite of jealousy.
confidence: a settled trust in oneself and one's abilities.
contempt: a cold, dismissive scorn for someone judged beneath you.
contentment: a quiet, self-sufficient satisfaction with things as they are.
courage: the resolve to face fear, danger or hardship.
curiosity: an eager itch to know, explore or find out.
cyberchondria: health anxiety stoked by looking up symptoms online.
delight: a bright burst of pleasure and joy.
depaysement: (French) the giddy disorientation of being far from home in an unfamiliar country.
desire: a strong wanting or longing for someone or something.
despair: the bleak collapse of all hope.
disappear: the wish to withdraw, to become invisible and unseen.
disappointment: the deflating let-down when hopes go unmet.
disgust: a visceral revulsion; the urge to recoil from something offensive.
dismay: sudden, disheartened alarm at an unwelcome turn.
dolce-far-niente: (Italian) the sweet, guiltless pleasure of doing nothing.
dread: a heavy, anticipatory fear of what is to come.
embarrassment: the flustered, blushing self-consciousness of being exposed.
empathy: the capacity to feel your way into another's emotions.
envy: a resentful longing for what someone else has.
euphoria: an intense, elated high of well-being.
exasperation: the frayed-patience irritation of being pushed too far.
excitement: an energised, quickened thrill of eagerness.
fago: (Ifaluk, Micronesia) a blend of compassion, love and sadness for someone in need.
fear: the alarmed response to danger or threat.
feeling-good: a glow of pride and pleasure in oneself.
formal-feeling: the numb, hollow composure that descends after a great grief.
fraud: the secret dread of being exposed as an impostor, undeserving of your success.
frustration: the vexed feeling of being blocked from what you want.
gezelligheid: (Dutch) the cosy, convivial warmth of being together in good company.
gladsomeness: a cheerful, gladdened lightness of spirit.
gratitude: warm thankfulness for a kindness received.
greng-jai: (Thai) the reluctance to impose on or trouble another person.
grief: the deep sorrow of loss, especially through death.
guilt: the gnawing sense of having done wrong.
han: (Korean) a collective, brooding sorrow and resentment born of long suffering.
happiness: a general sense of well-being, contentment and joy.
hatred: an enduring, intense hostility toward someone or something.
hiraeth: (Welsh) a wistful longing for a home or past that may never have existed.
hoard: the anxious urge to gather and keep possessions.
homefulness: the snug contentment of feeling settled and at home.
homesickness: the aching pull toward home when you are away from it.
hopefulness: a hopeful expectation that things will turn out well.
humble: a modest, unassuming sense of one's own smallness.
humiliation: the crushing shame of being lowered or degraded before others.
hwyl: (Welsh) a stirring, exuberant surge of emotional fervour and enthusiasm.
ijirashii: (Japanese) the moved, tender admiration for someone humble bravely overcoming hardship.
iktsuarpok: (Inuit) the restless anticipation that keeps you going outside to check whether someone is coming.
ilinx: the giddy, disorienting thrill of spinning, whirling or chaos.
indignation: righteous anger at unfairness or injustice.
inhabitiveness: a deep-rooted attachment to one's home and place.
insulted: the stung affront of being disrespected.
jealousy: the anxious fear of losing someone or something to a rival.
kaukokaipuu: (Finnish) a homesick longing for a faraway place you have never been.
liget: (Ilongot, Philippines) a fierce, energising passion — grief and anger channelled into vitality.
litost: (Czech) a tormented anguish of humiliation, self-pity and thwarted longing.
loneliness: the ache of feeling alone or cut off from others.
love: a deep affection, tenderness and attachment.
malu: (Indonesian/Malay) a shy, respectful abashment felt before those of higher status.
man: (Korean) a sorrow of unfulfilled longing and lingering regret.
matutolypea: a low, gloomy despondency that strikes only in the morning.
mehameha: (Tahitian) an eerie, uncanny dread of the numinous or otherworldly.
melancholy: a pensive, bittersweet sadness without obvious cause.
mono-no-aware: (Japanese) the tender, bittersweet awareness of the impermanence of all things.
morbid-curiosity: the compulsive fascination with death, danger or the gruesome.
mudita: (Sanskrit/Pali) a selfless, sympathetic joy in another's good fortune.
nakhes: (Yiddish) the glowing pride and joy a parent takes in a child's achievements.
nginyiwarrarringu: (Pintupi, Australia) the sudden fright that makes you start and look around.
nostalgia: a wistful, tender longing for the past.
oime: (Japanese) the uneasy weight of being indebted to someone.
overwhelmed: swamped, unable to cope with too much at once.
panic: a sudden, overpowering surge of fear.
paranoia: an anxious, suspicious sense of being watched or persecuted.
perversity: the wilful urge to do the very opposite of what is expected.
peur-des-espaces: (French) a fearful unease in vast, empty, open spaces.
philoprogenitiveness: an abundant, doting love of one's children and offspring.
pique: a flash of wounded pride and resentment.
pity: sorrow and sympathy for another's misfortune.
postal: an explosion of uncontrollable, murderous rage.
pride: a warm satisfaction in one's own or another's achievements.
pronoia: the delusive sense that the world is secretly conspiring in your favour.
regret: sorrow over something done or left undone.
relief: the loosening ease when a threat or strain passes.
remorse: the biting regret and self-reproach for a wrong.
reproachfulness: a wounded, accusing sense of having been let down.
resentment: a simmering bitterness over a perceived wrong.
ringxiety: the phantom sense that your phone is ringing or buzzing.
rivalry: the competitive edge of striving against another.
ruinenlust: (German) the pleasurable, melancholy delight taken in ruins.
sadness: a lowered, sorrowful heaviness of mood.
satisfaction: the fulfilled contentment of a desire met or a job done.
saudade: (Portuguese) a bittersweet, yearning nostalgia for someone or something absent.
schadenfreude: (German) the guilty pleasure taken in another's misfortune.
self-pity: an indulgent sorrow for one's own troubles.
shame: the painful sense of being flawed, unworthy or exposed.
shock: the stunned jolt of sudden, disturbing surprise.
song: (Ifaluk, Micronesia) a justified, righteous anger at a moral wrong.
surprise: the startled response to the sudden or unexpected.
suspicion: a wary mistrust that something is amiss.
technostress: the frazzled strain of coping with technology.
torschlusspanik: (German, 'gate-closing panic') the anxiety that time is running out and opportunities are closing.
toska: (Russian) a deep spiritual anguish and restless yearning, often without cause.
umpty: a sulky, out-of-sorts sense that everything is somehow all wrong.
uncertainty: the unsettled discomfort of not knowing.
vengefulness: the cold desire to repay a wrong with a wrong.
verguenza-ajena: (Spanish) the cringing, vicarious embarrassment felt on someone else's behalf.
viraha: (Sanskrit) the realisation of love awakened by separation from the beloved.
vulnerability: the exposed, unguarded openness to being hurt.
wanderlust: a restless longing to travel and roam.
warm-glow: the cosy inner glow of having done a good deed.
wonder: awed marvel at something beautiful, vast or mysterious.
worry: a fretful preoccupation with possible troubles.
zal: (Polish) a sorrowful blend of grief, regret and resigned longing.
